To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the polyhedral volume of a coordination polyhedron containing the lone-pairs of a cation is determined by the radius of the sphere of best fit to the anions, and by the distance of this sphere from the cation; the latter distance is a measure of the cation's lone-pair stereochemistry.

(1) the volume of a Te(IV) polyhedron is not a good indicator of its degree of distortion; (2) the volume of Te(IV) octahedron depends on its stereoactivity; and (3) the stereoactivity of the lone-pair is a key factor determining the flexibility of the polyhedron.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of stereoactivity on polyhedra containing lone-pair cations.
the effects of lone-pair electron pairs on the geometry of the coordination sphere, and the consequences of this for the properties of the solid state.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lone-pair stereoactive effect is not a distortion effect.
the lone pair in Te(IV) is not only stereoactive, but also very active.
the stereoactivity of lone pairs of electrons leads to an increase in polyhedron size, but that this effect is masked by a variety of other factors which are not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

polyhedral volume is determined by a balance of two opposing factors, the repulsive effect of the lone pair on the oxygen ligands (which tends to increase volume) and the tendency of the oxygen ligands to move away from one another in order to minimize their repulsion (which tends to decrease volume).
polyhedral volumes are not a reliable measure of distortion, but are strongly influenced by the degree of lone-pair localization and the distribution of the anions over the polyhedron surface.
the lone pair is not a rigidly defined entity, but is a flexible entity that can be localized to varying degrees, depending upon the local environment of the cation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the volume of a lone-pair coordination polyhedron is a function of the degree of stereoactivity of the cation's lone pair, and the degree to which the oxygen ligands are spread across the surface of a sphere of best-fit to the polyhedron.
the volume of an octahedron is not determined by its distortion.
